verses.sanskrit:
श्येन उवाच।
              धर्मात्मानं त्वाहुरेकं सर्वे राजन्महीक्षितः। सर्वधर्मविरुद्धं त्वं कस्मात्कर्म चिकीर्षसि॥१॥
verses.english: The Hawk said: All the kings of earth call you virtuous. Therefore why do you perform an act which is not in accordance with Dharma?

verses.sanskrit: विहितं भक्षणं राजन्पीड्यमानस्य मे क्षुधा। आ रक्षीर्धर्मलोभेन धर्ममुत्सृष्टवानसि॥२॥
verses.english: O king, I am oppressed by hunger; do not withhold from me my ordained food on the belief that you are thus gaining virtue, whereas you are not.

verses.sanskrit:
राजोवाच।
              संत्रस्तरूपस्त्राणार्थी त्वत्तो भीतो महाद्विज। मत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तः प्राणगृधुरयं द्विजः॥३॥
verses.english: The King said: O great bird, this one is afflicted with the fear of you; and desirous of escaping from you it has come in a fury to me for protection.

verses.sanskrit: एवमभ्यागतस्येह कपोतस्याभयार्थिनः। अप्रदाने परं धर्मं कथं श्येन न पश्यसि॥४॥
verses.english: O hawk, why do you not see that it is a great virtue for me not to give up this pigeon which has thus come to me?

verses.sanskrit: प्रस्पन्दमानः संभ्रान्तः कपोतः श्येन लक्ष्यते। मत्सकाशं जीवितार्थी तस्य त्यागो विगर्हितः॥५॥
verses.english: O hawk, this pigeon is seen to tremble with fear; it is agitated, it has come to me for protection of its life. It is not proper for me to forsake it.

verses.sanskrit: यो हि कश्चिद्द्विजान्हन्याद्गां वा लोकस्य मातरम्। शरणागतं च त्यजते तुल्यं तेषां हि पातकम्॥६॥
verses.english: He who kills a Brahmana and the mother of men (cow) and he who forsakes one who seeks his protection, both commit equal sin.

verses.sanskrit:
श्येन उवाच।
              आहारात्सर्वभूतानि संभवन्ति महीपते। आहारेण विवर्धन्ते तेन जीवन्ति जन्तवः॥७॥
verses.english: The Hawk said : O ruler of earth, all creatures exist on food. The animals are nourished and sustained by food.

verses.sanskrit: शक्यते दुस्त्यजेऽप्यर्थे चिररात्राय जीवितुम्। न तु भोजनमुत्सृज्य शक्यं वर्तयितुं चिरम्॥८॥
verses.english: A man can live many days even after forsaking his dear ones, but be cannot live long after abstaining from food.

verses.sanskrit: भक्ष्याद्वियोजितस्याद्य मम प्राणा विशांपते। विसृज्य कायमेष्यन्ति पन्थानमकुतोभयम् ॥९॥
verses.english: O king, my life will depart today if deprived of food. Leaving my body it would fearlessly go away to other ways.

verses.sanskrit: प्रमृते मयि धर्मात्मन्पुत्रदारादि नङ्क्ष्यति। रक्षमाणः कपोतं त्वं बहून्प्राणान्न रक्षसि॥१०॥
verses.english: O virtuous-minded one, at my death my wife and children will perish. By protecting the pigeon you do not (at all) protect many lives.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मं यो बाधते धर्मो न स धर्मः कुवर्त्म तत्। अविरोधात्तु यो धर्मः स धर्मः सत्यविक्रम॥११॥
verses.english: The virtue, that stands in the way of another virtue, is (really) unrighteousness. O truthful king, that virtue true virtue which is not conflicting.

verses.sanskrit: विरोधिषु महीपाल निश्चित्य गुरुलाघवम्। न बाधा विद्यते यत्र तं धर्मं समुपाचरेत्॥१२॥
verses.english: O ruler of earth, after comparing the opposing virtues and weighing their comparative merits, one ought to espouse that which is not opposing. Where there is no confliction, one should adopt that virtue which preponderates.

verses.sanskrit: गुरुलाघवमादाय धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये। यतो भूयांस्ततो राजन्कुरुष्व धर्मनिश्चयम्॥१३॥

राजोवाच।
              बहुकल्याणसंयुक्तं भाषसे विहगोत्तम। सुपर्णः पक्षिराट् किं त्वं धर्मज्ञश्चास्य संशयम्॥१४॥
verses.english: The King said : O excellent bird, as you speak words fraught with good, (may I ask) are you the king of birds, Suparna (Garuda)? I have not the least doubt that you are learned in all the precepts of virtue.

verses.sanskrit: तथा हि धर्मसंयुक्तं बहु चित्रं च भाषसे। न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचिदिति त्वां लक्षयाम्यहम्॥१५॥
verses.english: As you speak many and various words of virtue, I do not see there is anything in respect with it which you do not know.

verses.sanskrit: शरणैषिपरित्यागं कथं साध्विति मन्यसे। आहारार्थं समारम्भस्तव चायं विहंगम॥१६॥
verses.english: O bird, why do you consider, it virtuous to forsake one who seeks one's protection? Your attempt is only to search for food.

verses.sanskrit: शक्यश्चाप्यन्यथा कर्तुमाहारोऽप्यधिकस्त्वया। गोवृषो वा वराहो वा मृगो वा महिषोऽपि वा। त्वदर्थमद्य क्रियतां यच्चान्यदिह काङ्क्षसि॥१७॥
verses.english: You can appease you hunger with some other food which would be more plentiful. I am perfectly willing to procure for you any sort of food that would be palatable to you, whether it be an ox or a boar or a deer or a buffalo.

verses.sanskrit:
श्येन उवाच।
              न वराहं न चोक्षाणं न मृगान्विविधांस्तथा। भक्षयामि महाराज किं ममान्येन केनचित्॥१८॥
verses.english: The Hawk said: O great king, I am not desirous of eating a boar or an ox or any other kind of beasts. What have I to do with any other food?

verses.sanskrit: यस्तु मे देवविहितो भक्षः क्षत्रियपुङ्गव। तमुत्सृज महीपाल कपोतमिममेव मे॥१९॥
verses.english: O ruler of earth, O best of Kshatriyas, give me therefore this pigeon which is the food ordained to me by the celestials.

verses.sanskrit: श्येनः कपोतानत्तीति स्थितिरेषा सनातनी। मा राजन्सारमज्ञात्वा कद‌लीस्कन्धमासज॥२०॥
verses.english: O king, that the hawks eat the pigeons, is an eternal law. Do not get on a plantain tree not knowing its want of strength (to support you).

verses.sanskrit:
राजोवाच।
              राष्ट्रं शिबीनामृद्धं वै ददानि तव खेचर। यं वा कामयसे कामं श्येन सर्वं ददानि ते॥२१॥
verses.english: The King said : Oranger of skies, I am willing to give you this kingdom of my dynasty and all wealth and also all that you desire to have,
verses.bhavadeepa: कदलीस्कन्धमासजेति कदलीस्कन्धतुल्ये निःसारेऽस्मिन् धर्मे मा सज्जो भवेत्यर्थः ॥२०॥

verses.sanskrit: विनेमं पक्षिणं श्येन शरणार्थिनमागतम्। येनेमं वर्जयेथास्त्वं कर्मणा पक्षिसत्तम। तदाचक्ष्व करिष्यामि न हि दास्ये कपोतकम्॥२२॥
verses.english: O hawk, O excellent bird, with the exception of giving up this pigeon which has come to me for protection. Tell me what I shall have to do for the deliverance of this bird, I shall not give you this pigeon.

verses.sanskrit:
श्येन उवाच।
              उशीनर कपोते ते यदि स्नेहो नराधिप। आत्मनो मांसमुत्कृत्य कपोततुलया धृतम्॥२३॥
verses.english: The Hawk said : O Ushinara, O ruler of men, if you have so much affection for the pigeon, then cut a portion of your flesh and weigh it against this pigeon.

verses.sanskrit: यदा समं कपोतेन तव मांसं नृपोत्तम। तदा देयं तु तन्मह्यं सा मे तुष्टिर्भविष्यति॥२४॥
verses.english: O excellent king, when you flesh would be equal in weight with this pigeon, give it then to me and I shall be then satisfied.

verses.sanskrit: राजोवाच। अनुग्रहमिमं मन्ये श्येन यन्माभियाचसे। तस्मात्तेऽद्य प्रदास्यामि स्वमांसं तुलया धृतम्॥२५॥
verses.english: The King said : O hawk, I consider your this request as a favour. I shall give you my own flesh weighing it against the pigeon.

verses.sanskrit:
लोमश उवाच।
              उत्कृत्य स स्वयं मांसं राजा परमधर्मवित्। तुलयामास कौन्तेय कपोतेन समं विभो॥२६॥
verses.english: Lomasha said: O son of Kunti, O lord, cutting off his own flesh, that virtuous king weighed it against the pigeon.

verses.sanskrit: ध्रियमाणः कपोतस्तु मांसेनात्यतिरिच्यते। पुनश्चोत्कृत्य मांसानि राजा प्रादादुशीनरः॥२७॥
verses.english: But when he found that the pigeon was more heavy than this flesh (thus cut and placed in the scale), the king Ushinara again cut (some more) flesh (from his body) and placed it (in the scale).

verses.sanskrit: न विद्यते यदा मांसं कपोतेन समं धृतम्। तत उत्कृत्तमांसोऽसावारुरोह स्वयं तुलाम्॥२८॥
verses.english: When portion after portion of his flesh had been added to weigh against the pigeon and no more flesh was left on his body, he then himself mounted on the scale.

verses.sanskrit:
श्येन उवाच।
              इन्द्रोऽहमस्मि धर्मज्ञ कपोतो हव्यवाडयम्। जिज्ञासमानौ धर्मं त्वां यज्ञवाटमुपागतौ॥२९॥
verses.english: The Hawk said : O virtuous king, I am Indra. The pigeon is the carrier of the sacrificial Ghee (Agni). In order to test your virtuous merit, we came to your sacrificial grounds,

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते मांसानि गात्रेभ्य उत्कृत्तानि विशांपते। एषा ते भास्वती कीर्तिर्लोकानभिभविष्यति॥३०॥
verses.english: O king, as you have cut off your flesh from your body, your glory will be resplendent.

verses.sanskrit: यावल्लोके मनुष्यास्त्वां कथयिष्यन्ति पार्थिव। तावत्कीर्तिश्च लोकाश्च स्थास्यन्ति तव शाश्वताः॥३१॥
verses.english: O king, as long as men will speak of you on earth, so long will your glory endure and eternal region would be reserved for you.

verses.sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्त्वा राजानमारुरोह दिवं पुनः। उशीनरोऽपि धर्मात्मा धर्मेणावृत्य रोदसी॥३२॥
verses.english: Lomasha said: Having said this to the king, he (Indra) again went to heaven. And the virtuous Ushinara also, after filling heaven and earth with the merit of his pious deeds, went to heaven in an effulgent form. O king, yonder is the residence of that illustrious king.

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राजमानो वपुषाप्यारुरोह त्रिविष्टपम्। तदेतत्सदनं राजन्राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः॥३३॥
पश्यस्वैतन्मया सार्धं पुण्यं पापप्रमोचनम्। तत्र वै सततं देवा मुनयश्च सनातनाः। दृश्यन्ते ब्राह्मणै राजन्पुण्यवद्भिर्महात्मभिः॥३४॥
verses.english: Behold it which is holy and capable of cleansing sins. O king, here are always seen the celestials and eternal Rishis and also virtuous and high-souled Brahmanas.
